To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RNAi technology can effectively enhance the therapeutic efficacy PMX in an MPM xenograft model.
RNA interference of thymidilate synthase (TS) enhances the antitumour effect of pemetexed (PMX) both in vitro and, more importantly, in vivo in a malignant mesotheliomas xenograft mouse tumour model.
TS-shRNA lipoplex effectively enhanced the therapeutic efficacy of pemetrexet, the cornerstone of MPM chemotherapy, in vitro and in orthotopic mouse model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategy for the treatment of MPM, based on the combination of PMX and non-viral anti-TS shRNA, and the potential for its translation into the clinic.
the potential application of TS shRNA as an effective tool in the treatment of MPM.
the potential of RNAi to enhance the therapeutic efficacy and reduce the toxicity of PMX in the treatment of MPM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study demonstrates the feasibility of RNAi technology for enhancing the therapeutic effect of PMX in MPM.
TS RNAi embedded lipoplex can effectively enhance the antitumor activity of PMX both at the cellular and animal levels.

TS-shRNA lipoplex effectively enhanced the antitumoral effect of PMX via down-regulating TS in the MSTO cell line and that the combined treatment of TS-shRNA lipplex and PMX combated the progression and prolonged mouse survival in an orthotopically implanted MPM model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined treatment of TS shRNA liposome and pemetrexed efficiently combated the development of malignant pleural mesothelial tumors, compared to each treatment alone.
RNAi technology could be used to guide the downregulations of target genes in MPM, thereby, increasing the antitumor activity of PMX.
TS-shRNA lipoplex can be used as a potent tool to enhance the efficacy of PMX-based therapy against MPM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNAi-based gene silencing of TS can be a novel and effective therapeutic strategy for MPM.
the combination of PMX and anti-TS RNAi molecules can be considered as a novel therapeutic strategy to combat MPM.
RNAi technology can effectively enhance the therapeutic efficacy and safety of PMX, which is currently used in the treatment of MPM.
